correctness.rationale: For distinct a,b a positive triple forces c=a+lambda(b-a). In lexicographic atom order the six lambdas are t, 1/t, 1-t, (t-1)/t, 1/(1-t), and t/(t-1); none equals 0 or 1. Equal lambdas combine bits, and the null type occurs exactly when q^d exceeds two plus the orbit size. Solving the three involution and two order-three fixed-point equations gives the characteristic-three singleton, the equianharmonic pair, three separate harmonic mask patterns, and the generic sextuple. In a three-pebble move, only two positions are retained: either they are distinct and the mask support controls the response, or they coincide and all repeated-argument atoms reduce to the equality pattern. This proves permanence of partial isomorphism, not just bounded-rank agreement. Rank-three existential mask tests distinguish different rows. Direct field arithmetic independently reproduced all twelve table rows and multiplicities. The large characteristic-three class first occurs at 3^2, and generic-large needs at least nine points; the listed models attain both. Substituting into the four-variable chain gives (t-1)(t^2-t-1)=0, correctly separating the displayed sizes nine and eleven.
residual_risks: The replay is finite; unrestricted depth and exhaustiveness rely on the exact stabilizer analysis and back-and-forth proof. The representative bound is within the stipulated family.

value.rationale: This gives a test for every finite scalar Alexander model and all three-variable sentences at once. In this natural family the complete unrestricted equivalence collapses to rank-three tests, yet the harmonic orientations stay distinct and width four separates two models in a common class. The sharp sizes make this a precise benchmark for finite-variable logic, not a finite list of isomorphisms.
residual_risks: No classification is established for nonscalar quandles, function-symbol signatures, or counting logic.
